editorial:
Ever felt like you just don't fit in with the crowd? That is exactly where you find Kohei, a high schooler who would rather sleep at his desk and listen to the radio than deal with his loud classmates. The vibe is a mix of school drama and a touching life lesson. You get to see the tension between Kohei and the class clown, Takahashi, while the class rep, Katada, tries her best to help him out. It feels like a typical school day until Kohei meets Kakimoto, a homeless man who completely changes how he sees the world. It is a sweet, grounded story about finding a friend in the most unexpected place.

What really works here is the slow build of the friendship between the teen and the older man. The acting feels very real, and you can tell the characters actually care about each other. While the pace is a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. If you enjoy stories about unlikely bonds, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: By the end, Kohei learns that everyone has a story and a struggle, thanks to his bond with Kakimoto. He stops pushing people away and starts opening up to his classmates, especially Katada. The movie wraps up with Kohei finding a new sense of confidence and kindness. He realizes that being a hero does not mean being famous or popular, but simply helping others and being true to yourself.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about unlikely friendships and personal growth.
